data.summary: The six‑week plan front‑loads the weak Fluids unit, integrates a live class in week 3, and spreads the remaining units evenly while keeping each week to 4 hours. The final week is dedicated to mixed review and timed free‑response practice to build stamina before the October 13 exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce Fluids concepts and refresh basic kinematics.
tasks: Read the textbook sections for 8.1 and 8.2; create a one‑page summary of density and pressure definitions.
Do 10 free‑response questions on density and pressure, checking answers with the scoring guide.
Watch a short video on 1.1 and 1.2; sketch displacement‑time and velocity‑time graphs for three different motions.
Complete 5 practice problems on 1.1‑1.2, focusing on vector sign conventions.

weeks.focus: Complete Fluids unit and start Force & Translational Dynamics.
tasks: Read sections 8.3‑8.4; list three real‑world examples of fluid forces and conservation laws.
Solve 8.3‑8.4 problem set (8 questions), then compare solutions to answer key.
Review 2.1‑2.2 concepts; draw free‑body diagrams for two systems with multiple objects.
Complete 6 quantitative problems on center of mass and free‑body diagram analysis.

weeks.focus: Live class on Fluids and begin Work, Energy, Power.
tasks: Attend live class 10400; actively take notes on 8.1‑8.3 and ask one question.
After class, redo the class’s practice worksheet (5 problems) without notes.
Read textbook sections 3.1‑3.2; write a concise formula sheet for kinetic energy and work.
Do 8 free‑response questions covering 3.1‑3.2, grading with the AP scoring rubric.

weeks.focus: Linear Momentum and introductory Rotational Dynamics.
tasks: Watch a tutorial on linear momentum; solve 5 problems on 4.1‑4.2 (impulse and conservation).
Create a comparison chart of linear vs angular quantities (momentum vs angular momentum).
Study 5.1‑5.2; complete 6 rotational‑kinematics problems linking linear and rotational motion.
Do a mixed set of 4 free‑response questions (2 from momentum, 2 from rotational kinematics).

weeks.focus: Rotational Energy, Angular Momentum, and Oscillations.
tasks: Read sections 6.1 and 6.3; derive the rotational kinetic energy formula and angular impulse relation.
Complete 6 problems on rotational energy and angular momentum conservation.
Watch a video on simple harmonic motion; work through 5 problems on 7.1‑7.2 (period, frequency).
Finish a set of 4 free‑response questions that combine rotating systems with SHM concepts.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed free‑response practice.
tasks: Set a 90‑minute timer and complete a full‑length AP free‑response practice set (one question from each unit).
Mark answers using the official scoring guide; note any recurring errors.
Review error log; redo the three most missed problems with step‑by‑step solutions.
Create a one‑page “cheat sheet” summarizing key formulas and sign conventions for all units.

data.final_week_advice: Use the timed practice to simulate exam conditions, focus on pacing, and review your error log right before the test. Get plenty of rest the night before and arrive early to the testing center.
